claims: README.md and jlevy/squares#1001 (its comment of 09:29:26Z and its body as edited at 09:29:27Z) say the author ran exactsolve.py from evand/square-packing at 6067db5 (MIT) on all five packings in 80-digit arithmetic, and that it gave a result for four. At 127, 232, 264 and 305 it reports a KKT point (every contact force positive, balance residual 0) and a local minimum, its verdict 'local minimum of S, strict modulo N exact flat motions' with N = 52, 110, 155 and 132, so that none is rigid; the least contact forces are 6.66e-8, 7.28e-7, 6.75e-7 and 2.55e-6. At 204, whose load rests on 30 corner-on-corner touches, it found no smooth equilibrium and its Newton step diverged: no result in either direction.

They say the result is about the exact touching point near each witness (local-minimum/n-NNN-input.exact.txt), at sides 11.801753890364738880, 15.759531623540125992, 16.773807597982933201 and 17.945762359467513364, of which the witnesses are loosened copies, larger by 1.9e-11 to 4.0e-9; that at 232 the tool moved 22 loose squares into the contact system, the least gap between pairs that do not touch there 1.5e-12; and that the tool wrote its own rational certificate of each exact point (n-NNN-input.cert, its exact check VALID), whose lower sides they do not claim. They say the check is numerical, at 80 digits, and not a proof; that one tool by one author made it; that this repository's local_rigidity code was not run; and that the witnesses and their SHA-256 values are unchanged.

The README now reads 'They are upper bounds. We make no optimality claim.' where it read 'They are upper bounds only. We make no optimality or rigidity claim.', and its Not done list replaces 'No local-optimality, rigidity or KKT analysis.' with 'No local minimum result at n = 204.' and 'No proof of the local minimum results. They are numerical.' It says AI agents also ran the local minimum check, under JoeGun's direction. Those statements are the author's; no source program ran here.
